findings.title: Costs
findings.text: Slippage and commissions cost 0.062R per trade on average (+0.000R before costs, -0.062R after). Costs are affordable here.

findings.title: Win rate vs what's needed
findings.text: Win rate 37.6% against about 40.1% needed to break even with the actual average winner (+1.51R) and loser (-1.01R). Median target was 2.0R; only 20.8% of trades ever reached +2R before exiting.

findings.title: False breakouts
findings.text: 30.2% of stopped trades were stopped within 2 bars of entry: the move reversed almost immediately. Not unusually high.

findings.title: Giving back winners
findings.text: 18.0% of losing trades were up at least +1R at some point before turning into a loss. Few losers were ever meaningfully profitable, so exit management isn't the main problem.

findings.title: Stop placement
findings.text: 11.5% of stopped trades went on to reach the original target later the same day; 42.3% of those never went more than 1.5R against the entry first, so a somewhat wider stop might have held. Wider stops mean smaller positions, so this is a trade-off to test, not a fix.

findings.title: Long vs short
findings.text: Best: short +0.101R over 405 trades (95% interval [-0.177, 0.355]). Worst: long -0.234R over 387 trades (interval [-0.389, -0.09]).

findings.title: Trading with or against the trend
findings.text: Best: with trend +0.028R over 433 trades (95% interval [-0.13, 0.195]). Worst: against trend -0.207R over 250 trades (interval [-0.36, -0.034]).

findings.title: Time of day
findings.text: Best: 11:30-14:00 midday -0.012R over 270 trades (95% interval [-0.173, 0.158]). Worst: 14:00-16:00 afternoon -0.155R over 178 trades (interval [-0.337, 0.058]).

findings.title: Choppy markets
findings.text: Best: trending / expanding -0.062R over 685 trades (95% interval [-0.199, 0.088]). Worst: choppy / consolidating -0.065R over 107 trades (interval [-0.264, 0.148]).

findings.title: Late / extended entries
findings.text: Best: extended (>1.5 ATR from 9 EMA) -0.013R over 165 trades (95% interval [-0.366, 0.364]). Worst: near 9 EMA (<=1.5 ATR) -0.075R over 627 trades (interval [-0.185, 0.033]).

findings.title: Volume confirmation
findings.text: Best: volume confirmed -0.045R over 126 trades (95% interval [-0.385, 0.267]). Worst: weak volume -0.066R over 666 trades (interval [-0.18, 0.056]).

findings.title: Volatility
findings.text: Best: high-vol -0.043R over 319 trades (95% interval [-0.271, 0.17]). Worst: normal-vol -0.075R over 473 trades (interval [-0.17, 0.035]).

findings.title: Checklist score
findings.text: Best: checklist 50-69 -0.026R over 262 trades (95% interval [-0.198, 0.17]). Worst: checklist < 50 -0.106R over 316 trades (interval [-0.255, 0.053]).

findings.title: Setups that clearly lose
findings.text: level_breakout (long) (-0.407R, 71 trades); vwap_reclaim (long) (-0.582R, 47 trades). These are switched to NO TRADE in live signals.

findings.title: Setups with positive evidence
findings.text: None. No setup or ticker slice has an out-of-sample 95% interval entirely above zero.

diagnostics.caveat: These slices describe past out-of-sample trades. Choosing filters from them and re-testing on the same trades would be curve-fitting; any idea here must be confirmed on later data.

search.note: Each fold tried 12 parameter combinations on its training window and kept the best. The more combinations tried, the more the training winner is a lucky draw - which is exactly why only the following, unseen test window is reported.
